title: claude-tooling project configuration
description: Per-project configuration consumed by user-global wave meta skills. Lives at .claude/project.json in each consuming repo.

schemaVersion.description: Major schema version this file conforms to. Shared skills halt if this is below schema's minimumSchemaVersion.

projectName.description: Slug identifier used in logs, paths, and machine-facing reports (e.g. acme-web).

displayName.description: Short human-readable label used in cmux tab names and other UI surfaces (e.g. 'Acme Web', 'Acme App'). Kept short so tab strips remain readable when several projects are open.

repo.description: GitHub repo as owner/repo, used by gh CLI.

commandPrefix.description: Project-specific slash-command prefix for project-local skills (e.g. web, app). Meta skills always use /wave:.

stateDir.description: Repo-relative path to per-project wave state directory (e.g. .wave-state).

crossTabDir.description: Repo-relative path to cross-tab mailbox directory.

retroLog.description: Repo-relative path to the retro log markdown file.

waveStatusFile.description: Repo-relative path to the aggregate wave-status JSON file.

decisionLedger.description: Repo-relative path to the decisions ledger markdown file. Consumer brainstorm/analyst skills that allocate monotonic D-NNN IDs into this ledger MUST follow the reserve → write → release protocol in claude-tooling/docs/ledger-reservation-contract.md to prevent parallel-brainstorm ID collisions (FEEDBACK 2026-04-22 / 2026-04-24).

sessionTranscriptsDir.description: Absolute path to Claude Code session-transcripts directory for this project. Derived from the project's cwd hash by Claude Code.

checkCommand.description: Shell command that validates the repo (e.g. 'npm run check', 'composer test && npm run check').

buildCommand.description: Shell command that produces a production build.

builderRouting.description: Mapping from issue-category keys (e.g. frontend, schema, resource) to project-local builder skill names (e.g. build-frontend, build-resource). Keys are project-defined; values are skill names without the command prefix.

url.description: HTTP(S) endpoint that returns a JSON body describing prod health. The planner curl-fetches this on every invocation when configured.

healthyJqExpr.description: jq expression evaluated against the response body with `jq -e`. True = healthy. Example: '.status == "healthy"'. The planner passes this through a bash variable inside double quotes, so avoid literal `$` characters (shell parameter expansion will fire before jq sees the expression) — if you need jq variable bindings, file an issue so we can switch to `--arg` or a heredoc.

prodHealthProbe.description: Optional prod health probe. When present, planner Phase 1 fetches url and evaluates healthyJqExpr against the body; failure surfaces as BLOCKER in Phase 3 and routes Phase 4 toward amendment waves. When absent, the planner behaves as it did before v3 (no probe).

items.description: Repo-relative path to a dotenv file (e.g. 'payload/.env', 'apps/api/.env').

dotenvPaths.description: Optional list of dotenv paths to symlink from the main checkout into newly-created worktrees, in addition to the universal default of repo-root `.env`. Use this when the consumer's dev servers need env files at non-root locations (e.g. monorepo subprojects). Each entry must be a repo-relative path.

bootstrapCommand.description: Optional shell command run inside a freshly-created wave worktree to install dependencies and produce any generated artifacts the baseline check needs (e.g. 'composer install --no-interaction && npm install && npm run build'). A `git worktree add` checks out only tracked files, so gitignored vendored directories (vendor/, node_modules/) are absent and the wave's first baseline check fails on missing deps rather than on code. The planner runs this in Phase 5 Step 5.5a after creating the worktree; it must be idempotent (safe to re-run). When absent, no bootstrap step runs — appropriate only for consumers with no vendored dependencies.

applicationCodePaths.description: Optional list of git pathspecs identifying behaviour-bearing application code whose changes should be accompanied by an OpenSpec update. When set, the shared spec-drift CI workflow (claude-tooling/.github/workflows/spec-drift.yml) fails a pull request that touches any of these paths without also touching anything under `openspec/` (neither a spec edit under openspec/specs/ nor an active change under openspec/changes/). This is the T2.5 living-spec drift guard — see claude-tooling/docs/spec-drift-guard.md. When absent, the guard is a no-op, appropriate for consumers not using OpenSpec. Entries are git pathspecs matched against repo-relative paths, e.g. 'app', 'database/migrations', 'src/lib'.

label.description: Short human-readable name shown in the orchestrator's pre-merge gate prompt (e.g. 'Astro public site', 'Payload admin').

startCommand.description: Shell command run inside the wave worktree to start the dev server. May contain `cd` segments for monorepos (e.g. 'cd payload && npm run dev -- -p 3000'). Always pin the port explicitly — frameworks that auto-fall-back when the port is busy will silently move off the URL declared below.

url.description: URL handed to the human in the gate prompt. Must match the port pinned in startCommand.

readyProbe.description: Shell command that exits 0 once the server is ready to receive requests. Use `curl -sf <url>` so non-2xx responses are treated as not-ready. Do not rely on stdout string matching — neither Astro nor Next.js documents a stable ready-line format.

readyTimeoutSec.description: Maximum seconds to wait for readyProbe to succeed before failing the gate. 60 is enough for Astro; Next.js/Payload often needs 90 on cold start.

localPreview.description: Optional pre-merge local-preview gate. Each entry describes a dev server the orchestrator's Step 9b should start in the worktree before merging. The human is shown the URLs and asked to approve. When absent, Step 9b is skipped silently.
